archetypes.name: bash-safety
archetypes.rationale: The diff adds two new scripts with trap-based temp-file cleanup and a non-obvious cleanup_tmp boolean pattern; subtle lifetime mismatches won't surface in functional tests but could leak files or cause silent overwrites on interrupted runs.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the temp-file lifecycle in `scripts/read-result-env.sh` (the `cleanup_tmp` trap pattern near lines 491-501) and both callers in `skills/design/SKILL.md` Step 0-pre and Step 0b — confirm every error-exit path removes its allocated temp files and that `trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM` fires only after `mv` succeeds. In `skills/design/scripts/parse-design-argv.sh` `write_output_file`, verify the `rm -f "$tmp"` call in the `mv` failure branch covers the case where `mv` fails after the temp body is written. Check whether the early `validation_error "--output"` call in `parse-design-argv.sh` (invoked before `_output_path` is assigned) correctly skips output-file writing and does not dereference uninitialized argv variables in `write_output_body`. Verify Bash 3.2 compatibility of `scripts/read-result-env.sh` specifically: look for `local -a`, `mapfile`, `declare -n`, `${var^^}`, or `=~` patterns that are absent from its explicit constraint list. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: oos-blocked-by-logic
archetypes.rationale: The combine-issues SKILL.md adds blocked-by detection via a GitHub search query and wires add-blocked-by.sh; this is an orthogonal feature that changes issue disposition logic and may have search-precision issues or counting inconsistencies in the summary message.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the new OOS blocked-by detection step in `.claude/skills/combine-issues/SKILL.md` (the actuality-check diff, steps oos-2a through oos-2c). Evaluate whether `gh issue list --search "<bare-filename>"` is specific enough to avoid false positives — a generic name like `env.sh` or `utils.sh` would match many unrelated issues — and whether the instruction to scan titles and bodies is sufficient to filter them. Check the summary message: the plan appends `(<B> item(s) kept as blocked by in-flight implementing issues.)` — verify the instruction clearly defines how `<B>` is accumulated across all OOS issues, whether blocked items also count toward `<K>` (kept), and whether those counts are internally consistent. Confirm the `add-blocked-by.sh` failure path is unambiguous — the item must remain as actual/kept, not be silently dropped. Verify that blocked items flow correctly into the deduplication (oos-3) and combination (oos-4) steps without the blocked status causing silent omission. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
